coaching_overview:
**4-Week Base Building Block Summary (Aug 20 – Sep 16, 2026)**

This block establishes your aerobic foundation and training consistency after a relatively low-volume period (recent 14 days: ~24 km). Paces are derived entirely from your current Strava fitness (easy: 6:45/km, tempo: 5:56/km) with no target time specified.

**Phase Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4: Base Building** — all 4 weeks remain in Base Building phase due to no race date set. Once your race is confirmed, future blocks (Weeks 5–8) will transition to Aerobic Development, then Peak Training, then Taper/Race Week.

**Volume Progression:**
- Week 1: 42 km (establish baseline)
- Week 2: 46 km (+9.5%)
- Week 3: 48.5 km (+5.4%, peak week)
- Week 4: 37 km (−23.5%, recovery week)
- **Total block: 173.5 km**

**Key Features:**
- **Polarized training**: ~80% easy (Zones 1–2), ~20% hard (Zones 3–5)
- **Long run progression**: 11 → 13 → 15 → 12 km (steady growth with recovery cut)
- **Quality sessions**: 2 per week (tempo + VO2 max intervals), alternating intensities
- **Long run protection**: No hard sessions the day before or after Sunday long run
- **Training paces applied consistently**:
  - Easy: 6:45–7:00/km (warm-ups, cool-downs, long runs, recovery runs)
  - Tempo: 5:56/km (sustained lactate-threshold blocks: 6–7 km continuous)
  - VO2 max intervals: ~5:45/km (short repeats: 1.5–2 min with 90 sec–2 min recoveries)

**Monitoring & Adaptation:**
- Watch resting HR and perceived fatigue; if elevated mid-week, reduce easy run volume by 1–2 km
- Ensure 2–3 days between hard sessions to prevent consecutive-day fatigue
- Week 4 recovery is non-negotiable; resist urge to extend runs despite feeling good
- After Week 4, you will be well-prepared for Aerobic Development phase (marathon-pace work, progressive tempos, 20+ km long runs)

**Next Steps:**
- Confirm your target marathon race date → this will determine Weeks 5–16 periodization
- Continue tracking Strava data (HR, pace, elevation, perceived effort)
- Adjust easy-run paces by ±10–15 sec/km based on weekly fatigue signals
- Maintain 7 hours/week time budget; extend runs by 10–15 min (not distance) if time allows

**Total plan distance: 173.5 km over 4 weeks**
